deviations_from_design_section_2_2: [DecidableEq Bat] is NOT added to the variable lines: no proof needs the derived DecidableEq on PayloadCell Bat, and leaving it out keeps every decidability test on the local Classical.propDecidable (D26.3 memory rule).

Fintype: AffineLaw/AbsorptionLaw need [Fintype V] for V = Payload K Bat inside the law proofs. Fintype for PayloadCell (given [Fintype Bat]) and for R0Bat is derived in ZkStatement by `deriving instance`; [Fintype Bat] is an added instance binder on exactly 11 theorems: D12.payload_law, D12.hvzk_perfect_of_maskImage, Shift.payload_law_on, Shift.hvzk_on_good, Shift.hvzk_on_of, Hvzk.hvzk_conditional_of_maskImage, Hvzk.hvzk_perfect_of_maskImage, Hvzk.hvzk_zero_of_maskImage, FsGood.zkfs_of_maskImageOn_good_bridge, FsGood.zkfs_of_maskImageOn_good, FsAbort.zkfs_of_maskImageOn_abort. R0Bat is finite, so all instantiate at the R0 instance.

Bat is implicit and does not occur in the arguments of many definitions (MaskImage, MaskImageOn, HVZK_*, QPrime, BCond, ChainT0, ChainT0K4, silentMasks, ...); statements name it as (Bat := Bat), as §2.2 foresaw.
SilentReduction.batMap is valued in Bat → K (batRead replaces batProj), as §2.4/§4 recommend; BCond keeps its text.
ZkStatement.messages (the R0 32-row schedule) is stated for Payload K R0Bat.
